Hubris

HYOO-bris -- from ancient Greek hybris, 'excessive pride, insolence toward the gods'; the word's ultimate origin is still debated by scholars. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Hubris is exaggerated pride or self-confidence.

The captain's hubris convinced him the ship could outrun the storm, and he refused every warning to turn back.

Worked Example

Certain that his restaurant's reputation alone would keep customers coming no matter what, the owner stopped checking reviews, cut back on quality ingredients, and was shocked when the dining room emptied out within a year.

Hubris is the kind of excessive self-confidence that blinds someone to real risk -- the owner's certainty that nothing could touch his reputation is exactly what let the restaurant's quality quietly collapse.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

arrogance: an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or ability

conceit: excessive pride in oneself, often about one's own abilities

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

humility: a modest sense of one's own importance

modesty: the quality of not being excessively proud

Where it sits · how dangerously the pride swells — conceit → hubris → arrogance

conceit vs. hubris: Conceit often describes a more personal, vain pride in one's own looks or talent, while hubris carries a bigger, almost fateful weight, especially in stories where it leads to downfall.

arrogance vs. hubris: Arrogance describes a broader, everyday overbearing attitude toward other people, while hubris specifically names the excessive self-confidence that blinds someone to real danger.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — hybris

root — hybris: excessive pride, insolence toward the gods (Ancient Greek (ultimate origin disputed))

Put it together

Put it together: Hubris comes from ancient Greek hybris, describing a level of pride so extreme it was considered an insult to the gods themselves; its ultimate origin before that is still debated, and it survives in English today as a single, unbroken borrowed word with no common English relatives.

Use the root in a new word: nemesis

Use the root in a new word: nemesis: In Greek tragedy, a hero's hubris often summons a nemesis -- the very downfall he never saw coming.
